features.title: Document math settings
features.strategy: Defaults for all equations of the document (math font, break rules, margins, limits placement).
features.office: m:mathFont (a font with a MATH table, else Cambria Math), m:defJc, m:wrapIndent, m:wrapRight, m:intLim and m:naryLim apply to all equations of the document. Display equations break at the binary operators of their top level as m:brkBin says (measured with docx/local/mathset-a to -c, every line as in Word): before them (the default), after them, or both (repeat), a repeated minus shown as m:brkBinSub says ("--", "-+", "+-": the sign at the end of the line and the one at the start); an operator at a line's end keeps the space before it. m:lMargin and m:rMargin narrow the room of display equations, also without m:dispDef, which center in it (mathset-d). The equations of one m:oMathPara stand on one line one after the other. m:preSp, m:postSp, m:interSp, m:intraSp and m:smallFrac changed nothing in Word's printout (mathset-d).

features.title: VML shapes, text boxes and WordArt
features.strategy: The VML renderer of pptx `legacy.vml` (done), positioned in the text flow by the style attribute (mso-position-*) and w10:wrap; VML text boxes hold WordprocessingML like wps text boxes.
features.office: VML shapes (w:pict) are converted to Word drawings: rectangles, rounded rectangles, ovals, lines, preset shapes by o:spt, paths as custom geometries, groups (v:group: the children in its coordorigin and coordsize, nested), pictures (v:imagedata with crop), text boxes (v:textbox with its insets), WordArt (v:textpath), placed by the style attribute (position, margins, mso-position-*, rotation, flip, z-index) and w10:wrap (docx/local/vml-shapes, vml-group). A shape turns first and flips after, unlike DrawingML (docx/local/ vmlflip: triangles and connectors turned 30° and 90° with flip:x, flip:y and both; docx/external/libreoffice/ extras-ooxmlexport/n751117 79.1 → 88.4 %), a turn in fixed point (fd) counting 65536ths of a degree (docx/external/libreoffice/tdf137314_vml_rotation_unit_fd 61.8 → 99.7 %). A path's parameter left out before, between or after commas is 0 (m,128588; tdf105875_VmlShapeRotationWithFlip 1.8 → 99.3 %, core-ooxml-pass/vml-path 0.1 → 95.8 %, extras-ooxmlimport/tdf105143 3.5 → 100 %). A rounded rectangle's text stands inside its corners, as the DrawingML text rectangle says. An inline shape hangs from the top of its line (of its paragraph's space before on the first line), pictures stand on the baseline; an outlined shape takes the room of its box in whole 0.75 pt pixels, its outline and its shadow's offset right of and below it; spaces between drawings do not make their line taller (docx/local/vml-inline*). Fills and lines as Word draws them (docx/local/vml-fx, vml-angles, vml-pattern): a gradient runs, at the focus 0 Word writes by default, from color2 at the start of its angle (0: the top, 90: the left, 45: the top left corner, the angle applying in the shape stretched to a square) to the fill color, at focus 100 % the other way, at 50 % from the fill color to color2 in the middle and back, at -50 % the other way round, at any other focus the focus applied twice; a negative angle turns it round (the angle plus 180, the focus ±50 % reversed, any other the rest to 100 %); along its colors list where it has one; color2 "fill darken(n)" or "lighten(n)" for one-color gradients; gradientRadial from its focus position outwards; colors blend in linear light along an S-curve, in plain RGB along a straight line where the method is none or linear, and o:opacity2 fades color2 without tinting (within 3 of 255 of Word's pixels); pattern fills as their 8 × 8 bitmap, a point a bit, tiled from the page's corner; double and triple lines (linestyle), line opacity, shadows (v:shadow: an unblurred copy at its offset, 2 pt right and down by default, in its color and opacity, a double shadow's second in color2 at offset2 behind it). Word 97 borders (w10:bordertop, borderleft, borderbottom, borderright) frame the shape outside, width/8 pt each floored to Word's 0.12 pt dots, double lines three times that, dotted and dashed ones dashed (docx/local/vml-border). w10:anchorlock only locks the anchor while editing. A floating shape's shadow widens its extent on its side, which alignment counts (docx/local/sa-v*: a shape centered at the page's top with a shadow 80 pt left and 36 pt up stands 40 pt right and 36 pt down; docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/testOuterShdw); mso-wrap-distance-* keep wrapped text away (9 pt left and right, none above and below by default); a text box with mso-fit-shape-to-text is as high as its text where it is drawn. Known deviations: a perspective shadow's matrix is left out; the text wraps the stated height of a box fitted to its text.

features.title: HTML output
features.strategy: One self-contained HTML file: fixed-size page boxes with absolutely positioned glyph runs, SVG for drawings, embedded fonts and pictures; print CSS keeps one page per sheet.
features.office: One self-contained HTML file: a fixed-size section per page with a named @page per paper size (printed, every page keeps its size), text as SVG text at our positions in the fonts we measured with (fonts the browser cannot find by name, such as Office cloud fonts, embedded), drawings, charts, SmartArt and equations as SVG, pictures embedded, bookmarks as anchors and hyperlinks as links. Printed, outlines keep their width: the crisp edges that shapes have on screen (as PowerPoint draws axis-aligned lines) would make Chrome print their strokes as hairlines of width 0, which PDF renderers and printers draw thinner and lighter than Word's 0.75 pt (docx/external/powertools/WC/WC065-Textbox 70 → 88.6 %; of 306 documents with such outlines 83 better, 40 more over 90 %).

features.office: Pages, columns, sections, headers and footers and the paragraph keep rules match Word's line positions within 0.1 pt on the generated documents (word-lines); tables break between rows and split rows at lines, repeat their header rows, keep rows that may not split and rows whose paragraphs keep with the next (docx/local/tblpages: 229 lines, mean 0.06 pt); footnotes share the page with their references and continue on the next (note.footnotes); floating objects stay on their anchor's page (engine.floats).

features.title: Line layout
features.strategy: The text engine of pptx `engine.textLayout` (done) extended by Word's rules: line height from the font's metrics and line spacing, tabs, justification, East Asian grid and kinsoku, hyphenation, inline objects, lines shortened by floating objects.
features.office: Lines break at UAX #14 opportunities with Word's kinsoku, and at every space before a character that is not East Asian, also before periods, closing brackets and quotes, slashes and percent signs (docx/local/ spacebreak: 19 characters), after every hyphen and en dash whatever stands before it, digits, punctuation or a space, after the hyphen U+2010 from Word 2013 on, not after slashes, plus signs, underscores or non-breaking hyphens (docx/local/hyphbreak-15, -12: 19 cases), and before and after inline pictures as beside ideographs (docx/local/tblpic3); a word longer than the line breaks between characters, on the line where it begins if nothing but a tab or a list number stands before it there, with at least one character after a number, none needed after a tab (docx/local/lw-*, lx-*, ly-*, lt-*: modes 14 and 15); a tab goes to the next line with the word after it where that word does not fit (lw-6 to lw-10, ly-1, ly-4; docx/external/ libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/tdf123054, tdf142404_tabOverMarginC15); trailing spaces hang past the end; spaces never make a line taller or lower, whatever their size or place, and a line of only spaces is the paragraph mark's (docx/local/ts-*, tu-*, tv-*: a 45 pt space before, between or after 9 pt words leaves the line 9 pt in modes 12 to 15, a 45 pt "x" or no-break space does not); tabs neither, a paragraph's last line of only tabs is the mark's, a line before it of a tab alone the tab's (docx/local/tabheight: a 24 pt tab alone, twice or between 8 pt letters leaves an 8 pt mark's line 8 pt, an 8 pt tab alone a 24 pt mark's 24 pt; tovc-10: a 10 pt tab wrapped past the right indent before 12 pt text keeps its line 10 pt); justified lines squeeze spaces for one more word where that changes them less than stretching would (paragraph.basic); automatic hyphenation breaks words as Word does (paragraph.hyphenation); line grids snap lines to whole pitches (section.docGrid); East Asian spacing and alignment (paragraph.eastAsian). Glyphs are drawn as browser text at positions from our layout; Word's PDF and ours go through the same rasterizer, so equal positions give equal pixels. Punctuation compression changed nothing in Word's printout (docx/local/ec-*).

features.title: Floating objects and text wrapping
features.strategy: Anchored objects, frames and floating tables are placed first, then lines are broken into the space around them; objects anchored in later text may move earlier lines, so layout iterates until stable.
features.office: Floating drawings are placed on their anchor's page and the page is laid out again around them until it is stable (at most four runs); from Word 2013 an object that wraps text and moves with its paragraph takes the paragraph to the next page where it would reach past the bottom margin, a box that resizes to its text at least as high as Word saved it (docx/local/af-over, af-over-tb, af-huge go; af-fit, af-over-none in front of the text, af-over-page, af-over-margin and af-over-14 stay; docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/ tdf123243, tdf115719 20 → 100 %, tdf137655 54.2 → 100 % of the lines); lines are broken into the segments beside the objects, words that do not fit a segment continue in the next one, lines with no room move down below the object (docx/generated/wrapping, wrap-types), below the first of the objects beside them to end (td-1), beside objects wrapped along their polygons a line at a time, so on the paragraph's line pitch (ub-*), and to the next page where they do not fit below it. A segment takes text from 18 pt, also an empty line's, the first of a line only where the line's first word fits (docx/local/tf-*, tk-*, tq-*, te-*, tg-*, th-*, tl-*: 17.3 pt stay empty, 19.3 take "a an", a word of 40.6 pt goes below an object leaving 39.3 pt); before Word 2013 a line beside objects wrapped square stays where the column has 18 pt beside them, also only outside its indents, takes what of it they leave, a character a line where none, a word breaking where it does not fit (tx-*, ty-*, tz-*, ua-*; powertools/RP/RP001-Tracked-Revisions-01-Accepted), and beside objects wrapped along their polygons a segment takes text from 9 pt (tv-*, tw-*; core-text/fly-minimal-wrap). A line moved down for the height of its paragraph mark stands where it fits with its own (uitest/tdf124675). A paragraph whose own object leaves it no room on the page moves on with the object, and the page it left is laid out without it (docx/local/anchorpush-*). An object kept free above and below that reaches down to its paragraph's place pushes the lines already in the column that it overlaps below it; where its paragraph would then no longer begin in the column, or where the object ends above the paragraph, it takes the paragraph to the next (uc-1 to uc-5, ud-*; generated/wrapping, local/compat11-wrapping; extras-layout/fdo43573-2-min). Objects beside the column leave its lines alone, also those kept free above and below, and a paragraph going on in another column or page goes on beside the objects there (fdo43573-2-min: an image at the top of a page's left column, the right column's text and the last line of a paragraph from the page before). Text frames and drop caps (paragraph.frames) and floating tables (table.floating) take part in the same exclusions. A table does not stand beside the floating objects and frames before it: it begins below every one its part on the page would overlap, from Word 2013 on whatever their wrapping, before only those kept free above and below (docx/local/fx-1 to fx-13, ft-1 to ft-8: below a 40 pt shape wrapped square or top and bottom, also one beside a 70-row table's last rows on the page, and below frames not beside text, anchored to the text or the page; a shape right of the table and one without wrapping leave it; docx/external/tika/testWORD_tableInRunInsideParagraph, docx/external/libreoffice/core-ooxml-pass/ fdo78904_fileHang); below a floating table of the text only where it does not fit beside it and reaches its box, its distances aside (ib-1 to ib-7: a table of 90 pt beside one of 350 pt, of 468 pt below it; writerfilter-dmapper/floattable-then-table, extras-layout/tdf167526; extras-ooxmlexport/tdf92157: a table into the distance of a floating table in the right margin stays). A floating table that may not overlap others (w:tblOverlap never) moves right of the one before it that it would overlap where it fits, else below it (table.floating). Known deviations: a table that fits beside a floating table Word moves beside it (ib-1, ib-2), ours stays at its place across it; in mode 14 Word sets a table beside a shape wrapped square, indented and narrower (fx-5), ours stays over it; a table whose cells' paragraphs have frame properties stands in that frame at its position (lb-1 to lb-4, tdf104394_lostTextbox), ours in the text.

features.title: Table layout
features.strategy: Word's autofit algorithm, measured against generated tables, and rows that span pages.
features.office: Word's autofit: each column's minimum and maximum width with margins (the maximum capped at 1584 pt); preferred widths fixed, giving way where they do not fit; the maxima when they fit, else the minima and the rest in proportion to max - min, else the content minima shrunk (table.width); fixed layout by the grid; rows that split across pages unless cantSplit, repeated header rows, nested tables (docx/local/tbl-autofit 92/92 lines, docx/generated/tables 44/44).

features.title: Font resolution and fallback
features.strategy: As pptx `engine.fonts` (done) with Word's font substitution (font.table).
features.office: Installed, embedded and Office cloud fonts (Aptos) as in pptx, with Word's own substitution of missing families (font.table) and theme fonts (font.theme). A character the run's font lacks is measured and drawn in the font Word falls back to, by range: emoji Segoe UI Emoji (also before U+FE0F); symbols, dingbats, arrows and Braille Segoe UI Symbol; letterlike and mathematical symbols, technical symbols and enclosed numbers Cambria Math (enclosed letters then MS Gothic or MS Mincho); geometric shapes Arial; Thai, Lao and Khmer Leelawadee UI; Indic scripts Nirmala UI; Georgian Sylfaen; Ethiopic Ebrima; Cherokee Gadugi; Syriac Segoe UI Historic; Tibetan Microsoft Himalaya; Myanmar Myanmar Text; Hangul Malgun Gothic or Batang beside serif and East Asian fonts; Chinese characters and kana MS Mincho, then PMingLiU or Microsoft JhengHei; Hebrew and Arabic outside right-to-left runs Arial, Times New Roman beside serif fonts (docx/local/thd2-a, thd2-b; docx/external/poi/rtl 62.9 → 91.9 %). Lines grow with the fallback's metrics as in Word; spaces and format characters stay in the run's font, marks with their base (docx/local/fallback-arial 96.1 %, fallback-calibri 95.7 %, fallback-times 97 %, every line within 0.1 pt). Color emoji are Chrome's (COLRv1 shading) where Word draws them flat.

features.title: Fidelity measurement
features.strategy: Word (COM) exports every reference document to PDF; its pages are rasterized and compared with our pages like the PowerPoint references, on documents Word generates by COM and on external test documents.
features.office: Word (COM) exports every reference document to PDF; Chrome prints our HTML to PDF and the same rasterizer (Windows.Data.Pdf) renders both, page by page at 96 dpi, for the pixel and SSIM scores; pdf-text and word- lines compare Word's PDF layout with ours line by line and glyph by glyph. 29 documents generated by Word through COM (docx/generated, 92.6 % overall) and local probes for each measured rule. The rasterizer ignores the soft masks Chrome writes (reflections, soft edges), which MuPDF shows.
